root_cause.text: The idxd event log cleanup path in `idxd_device_evl_free()` incorrectly depended on the volatile hardware `GENCFG.evl_en` register state to decide whether to free `idxd->evl`, so a device reset during removal cleared the register and caused the allocated event log memory to be skipped and leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `ioread32(... IDXD_GENCFG_OFFSET)` and `if (!gencfg.evl_en) return;` checks, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that device reset during remove zeros the configuration registers, making the “event log support was enabled” check fail even though `idxd->evl` was still allocated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always run EVL cleanup when an EVL object exists instead of skipping it based on the GENCFG EVL enable bit.
intent_record.what: The change removes the read of the GENCFG register and the early return that skipped the function when gencfg.evl_en was not set, leaving the function to always proceed to lock evl->lock, clear gencfg.evl_en, and write gencfg.bits back whenever evl is present.
intent_record.how: At runtime, idxd_device_evl_free() no longer exits based on the current hardware EVL enable bit and will always execute the EVL disable/write path for an existing evl structure, ensuring the cleanup sequence is performed instead of being skipped when the register reports EVL as disabled.

grouping_result.intent: Always run EVL cleanup when an EVL object exists instead of skipping it based on the GENCFG EVL enable bit.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by removing dependence on the volatile GENCFG.evl_en hardware state and ensuring EVL cleanup/free happens whenever idxd->evl exists, preventing the memory leak after reset during removal.

candidates.rationale: This conditional made EVL cleanup depend on the hardware GENCFG EVL enable bit. After a reset cleared the volatile register, cleanup was skipped even though idxd->evl was still allocated, causing the leak.
This early return is the action that actually skipped freeing the allocated event log object when gencfg.evl_en was cleared by reset.
Reading the volatile hardware register introduced the faulty dependency on transient device state during teardown, enabling the later incorrect skip of cleanup.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional is the direct vulnerable decision point: it gates EVL cleanup on the volatile hardware GENCFG.evl_en bit instead of whether idxd->evl is allocated. After reset clears the register, this condition becomes true and causes cleanup to be skipped, leaking the event log memory.
This early return is the concrete action that skips freeing idxd->evl once the faulty GENCFG-based condition is met, causing the leak during device removal after reset.
This statement reads the volatile hardware register and introduces the improper dependency on transient device state in the teardown path, enabling the later incorrect decision to skip EVL cleanup.
